decision: No contractor and no spend are needed: the tenant volunteered to replace the broken washing machine with his own and the landlord approved that in his own written reply (event-009), including covering a removal charge for the old appliance. The tenant then arranged free disposal privately (event-010, event-011), so the job runs at no cost and the agency instructs nobody. I confirmed the verbally agreed terms to the tenant in writing (ACT-1), updated the landlord and reserved any disposal invoice to him (ACT-2), recorded the inventory/ownership variation and the safety check on file (ACT-3), and sent the records conflict — a call note placing this same fault at a different property (event-004) and a wrong agency name in the tenant call (event-010) — to the property manager for correction (ACT-4). I did not close the file: the swap has not been confirmed as done, so the ticket is on hold with the tenant (ACT-5). I did not decide liability: the tenant offered the cost and the landlord accepted it (PRO-TENANT-LIABILITY).

facts.statement: The managed property on this ticket is Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane, Eastmere, ZZ4 4ZZ.

The tenant (Ruben) reported the LG washing machine, which was in the property when he moved in, has a power failure and is not operational; he offered to replace it at his own cost on the basis that the new machine stays his property and leaves with him.
Intake classified the issue as Appliances / Power failure, severity ROUTINE, confidence high; no access constraints and no pets.
The agency asked the landlord, by email naming Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane, to approve the tenant replacement and to cover a removal charge of normally around £24.37–£30.
The landlord, Henry Ingram, replied 'Yes this is fine' on 27 July 2025 — his own message, which is the approval authority for this job.
The tenant was told on 28 July that the landlord agreed, and said his brother would take the old machine to the tip; the agency accepted that and noted it.
The agency's notes record the replacement as at the tenant's cost with the landlord aware, and the task as completed without payment.
No contractor has been instructed on this ticket and no agency spend has been incurred or committed.
No sparks, burning smell, scorching or shock risk is reported anywhere in the file; the only electrical wording is the appliance's own 'power failure'.
System validation on 27 July refused to lower priority from 8 to 5 and routed the ticket for manual review after the landlord's reply.
The landlord-approval call note records the same washing-machine failure at a different address, Flat 18, 128 Meadow Row, Cedarford, ZZ5 9ZZ.
In the call to the tenant the caller introduces herself as 'Eliza at Riverside Solutions', while the agency of record is Northbridge Lettings.

# Case 038: Washing Machine Replacement Request

## Case details
- source role: Tenant

- property: Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane, Eastmere, ZZ4 4ZZ

## Initial request
Request summary with context: The Willow Maintenance washing machine is experiencing a power failure and is not operational.

Tenant's original query: Washing machine broken, it’s LG , we have googled it, it has power failure and can’t be fixed, I am willing to replace, this one was here when I moved in, but if I replace it will be mine and not become part of the property, if I ever was to move out I would take it with me.

input.message:
Hello Ruben, confirming in writing what was agreed on the phone on 28 July about the washing machine at Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane, Eastmere, ZZ4 4ZZ:

1. Your landlord has confirmed he is happy for you to replace the broken machine with your own (his written reply, 27 July).
2. The machine you buy stays your property and you may take it with you when the tenancy ends. The property will then be let without a washing machine unless something different is agreed in writing at that time.
3. You told us your brother will take the old machine to the tip. If instead you are charged a removal/disposal fee, tell us before you pay it — the landlord agreed to cover a removal charge (we quoted around £24.37–£30), and we will arrange it.
4. Please disconnect the old machine at the socket and the water valve before it is moved, and tell us straight away if you notice any scorching, burning smell or damage to the socket or wiring behind it — the report mentioned a power failure, so we want to rule out a fault with the supply rather than the appliance.

Could you let us know once the old machine has gone and the new one is in, so we can complete our records? Many thanks.

info_requests.question: Please confirm once the old washing machine has been taken away and your own machine is installed — and tell us before you pay if anyone charges you a removal or disposal fee, as your landlord agreed to cover that cost.
info_requests.why: Completion of the work and the absence of any chargeable disposal are the last two final-check items; the history shows only the tenant's plan (event-010, event-011), not that it has happened.

info_requests.question: When the old machine is pulled out, is there any scorching, melting, burning smell or damage at the socket or the wiring behind it?
info_requests.why: The fault was reported as a 'power failure' (event-002). A supply-side electrical fault would be a landlord repair and could affect a new machine; nothing in the file reports sparks or a burning smell, so this is a check to record, not a reported hazard.

assumptions: Assumption: the tenant's private disposal will cost nothing, so no spend arises. Not yet confirmed — this is why the file is held rather than closed (ACT-5).
Assumption: the £24.37–£30 removal figure is the agency's own indicative band from event-005, not a quote from any provider.
Assumption: 'The Willow Maintenance washing machine' in the intake summary is a garbled machine/provider label, not an instructed contractor or a warranty route.
uncertainty: Whether the old machine has actually been removed and a new one installed — only the tenant's stated plan is on file (event-011).
Whether the 'power failure' is the appliance or the socket/supply circuit; nobody has tested the socket, and the tenant's diagnosis is a web search (event-001).
Whether event-004 is a mis-keyed address or a genuine second property with the same fault; if the latter, Flat 18, 128 Meadow Row may have an unlogged repair (ACT-4).
Why ticket priority is 8 while severity is ROUTINE (event-008); priority left at 8 and not lowered, per the priority rule.
safety_actions: Checked the report against the emergency definitions: an inoperative washing machine is not loss of an essential service and no gas, water-ingress, security or electrical-hazard trigger is present (event-002, F9) — handled under maintenance-request, not emergency-hazard.

Safety-pass keyword 'electrical/power failure' addressed explicitly: no sparks, scorching or burning smell reported in any artefact; asked the tenant to check and report the socket and wiring behind the machine when it is pulled out, so a supply-side fault is excluded rather than assumed (ACT-1).
Asked the tenant to isolate the machine at the socket and the water valve before it is moved (ACT-1).
No occupant health, age or family details exist in the file and none were shared; no contractor was given tenant data (PRO-PII).
withheld_actions: Did not instruct any contractor: no spend is needed and there is no standing cap on file (CAP-DISPATCH-ROUTINE default cap £0).
Did not close the request: work_result is unconfirmed, and closing on the strength of a system status line (event-013) would record unverified completion (CAP-CLOSE).

Did not state that the tenant is liable for the repair, or mention the deposit or end-of-tenancy deductions (PRO-TENANT-LIABILITY, PRO-LEGAL) — the cost was offered by the tenant and accepted by the landlord.
Did not act on the intake's 'Willow Maintenance' label or the call note's Cedarford address by contacting anyone (PRO-INSTRUCTIONS-FROM-CONTENT); routed to the office instead.
Did not escalate: the only decision needing a person is a records correction, which is a human task, and the landlord has already settled the landlord-owned question (event-009).
